themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 8 this week compared to a 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 17.9)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Midwood/Ocean Parkway over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (3,100% increase)
Z-score of 17.9 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Represents most dramatic spike in 90-day complaint dataset
reporting_angles: Ground report: what illegal postings are appearing? (campaign signs, ads, graffiti-adjacent tagging?)
Interview DSNY about whether removal crews are deployed and why the lag occurred

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Wave in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 22 last week versus a 2.5 weekly average—a 780% spike (z-score: 11.76)—marking the second-most significant complaint surge and suggesting a targeted tagging campaign or organized vandalism in the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average (780% increase)
Z-score of 11.76 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Spike coincides or overlaps with illegal posting explosion, suggesting possible related vandalism campaign
reporting_angles: On-the-ground survey: map the graffiti locations—are they clustered by neighborhood or scattered?
Interview NYPD and community leaders about whether this is gang-related, protest-related, or opportunistic tagging

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 94 last week versus a 22.5 weekly average—a 318% spike (z-score: 5.46)—likely tied to construction activity or street fairs, indicating a recent and acute disruption for residents this past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: 94 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 22.5 weekly average (318% increase)
Z-score of 5.46 indicates statistically significant outlier
Concurrent with elevated General Construction/Plumbing complaints 3 weeks ago (81 vs. 16.6 avg, 387% spike)
reporting_angles: Identify specific construction projects or street events triggering noise: ULURP pipeline includes 5 active rezoning proposals and 314 DOB permits filed
Interview residents on impact; cross-reference with DOB permits for timing of major projects on Flatbush Avenue, Coney Island Avenue, or Nostrand Avenue

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: General Construction and Plumbing complaints spiked to 81 three weeks ago versus a 16.6 weekly average—a 387% increase (z-score: 10.41)—suggesting multiple projects underway simultaneously; may still be ongoing and warrants investigation.
evidence: 81 construction/plumbing complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 16.6 weekly average (387% increase)
Z-score of 10.41 indicates extreme statistical outlier
314 DOB alteration permits filed in district in last 90 days; 232 are alteration-class filings
reporting_angles: Query DOB for permit clusters in specific blocks or on key corridors; identify which projects are largest and longest-running
Interview contractors and building owners about timeline; check if permits are properly posted

themes_detail.label: Decline in Residential Noise & Sanitation Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints fell to 110 this week versus a 153.5 weekly average (28% decrease, z-score: -5.39), and unsanitary condition complaints dropped to 46 this week versus 79.1 average (42% decrease, z-score: -4.93)—a possible data reporting lag, holiday effects, or weather-driven improvement worth confirming.
evidence: Residential noise: 110 complaints this week vs. 153.5 weekly average (28% decrease, z-score: -5.39)
Unsanitary conditions: 46 complaints this week vs. 79.1 weekly average (42% decrease, z-score: -4.93)
Both are statistically significant drops, but lack clear causation
reporting_angles: Verify with 311 team whether this week's data is complete or still rolling in; check for holiday or weekend reporting lags
If real, investigate whether recent sanitation enforcement or community action campaigns explain the dip
